claims.claim: Pepero Day is observed on Nov 11 in South Korea; this article offers original low-equipment DIY ideas and avoids claiming a historical origin or commercial ranking.
Food label information can identify allergens; consumers should check the package for ingredients and allergen statements, particularly when gifting homemade food.
The recipe ideas are suggestions, not tested recipes; ingredient proportions and setting time vary by product and room temperature.

sources.title: Exploring Korea's Holidays: Pepero Day
sources.body: Republic of Korea official site describes Pepero Day as observed on November 11 and identifies the contemporary gift-giving custom. Background only, not evidence for sales ranking or definitive historical origin.

sources.title: 식품 알레르기 예방법
sources.body: Food Safety Korea guidance: check allergen labeling before purchase and ask whether foods contain allergens. For homemade gifts, ingredient list and cross-contact limitations should be disclosed.

cannotSay: Do not call any brand or kit the best-selling product or recommend based on unsupported sales data.
Do not claim a recipe has been personally tested.
Allergen labeling on a commercial package is not a guarantee against cross-contact in a home kitchen; mention this plainly.
No fixed chocolate melt or set time; follow package directions and tempering instructions if present.
